title: Superlinear Boolean circuit lower bounds
formal:
Does there exist one total, length-preserving, deterministic polynomial-time function
\[F:\{0,1\}^{*}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{*},\qquad |F(x)|=|x|,\]
whose unrestricted Boolean circuit complexity is not linear? Precisely, writing \(F_n:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}^{n}\) for its restriction to inputs of length \(n\), the requested lower bound is
\[\forall C>0\ \forall N\ge1\ \exists n\ge N:\quad \operatorname{CC}(F_n)>Cn.\]
Here \(C\) is real and \(N,n\) are integers. Preserve the card's polynomial-time meaning of “explicit” and its allowance of \(n\) output bits. The lower bound need only exceed every fixed linear bound at arbitrarily large lengths.
definitions:
A binary string is a finite sequence of bits; \(\{0,1\}^{*}\) contains all such strings, including the empty string. Length preservation requires exactly \(n\) output bits on an \(n\)-bit input, and the empty output on the empty input. Polynomial-time computation means that a single deterministic multitape Turing machine, with no advice or oracle, outputs \(F(x)\) and halts on every input \(x\) within \(a(|x|+1)^d\) steps, for fixed constants \(a\ge1\) and integer \(d\ge1\). Writing the output counts toward the running time.

For each fixed \(n\), a competing circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with \(n\) input wires, optional free constants 0 and 1, gates computing arbitrary Boolean functions of at most two input bits, and an ordered list of \(n\) output wires. This is the full \(B_2\) basis: all two-input truth tables are allowed, including AND, OR, XOR and functions that ignore an input; unary NOT is also allowed. Each gate contributes one unit of size. Inputs, constants and output designations contribute zero. A wire may feed arbitrarily many gates or output positions, and intermediate gates may be shared by several outputs. Depth is unrestricted. An output may be an input wire, a constant or a gate output.

The circuit computes \(F_n\) exactly if its ordered output vector equals \(F_n(x)\) for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\). The number \(\operatorname{CC}(F_n)\) is the minimum gate count of any such circuit. Competing circuits are nonuniform: the choice at each length is independent, and no algorithm is required to construct their descriptions. In contrast, the polynomial-time algorithm for \(F\) must work uniformly at all lengths. This distinction is part of the target.

The statement \(\operatorname{CC}(F_n)=O(n)\) means that there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(N\ge1\) such that \(\operatorname{CC}(F_n)\le Cn\) for every integer \(n\ge N\). The displayed target is its exact negation. It does not require \(\operatorname{CC}(F_n)/n\) to tend to infinity at every sufficiently large length. The function, its program and its running-time polynomial are chosen before all the lower-bound quantifiers.

The source uses AND, OR and NOT gates and leaves “explicit” broad. Every full-basis gate has a constant-size AND/OR/NOT implementation, and those gates are already allowed in \(B_2\). Thus changing between these two fixed bases changes minimum size by at most a constant factor and preserves the not-\(O(n)\) target. The polynomial-time explicitness convention is the previously recorded specialization of the source; it is not claimed to be equivalent to every possible meaning of “explicit.” No linearity or other algebraic restriction is imposed on \(F\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated existence claim. A positive answer must specify one total length-preserving function, prove that one uniform deterministic algorithm computes it in polynomial time, and prove the displayed lower bound against every circuit in the full model. A negative answer must show that every such polynomial-time function has \(O(n)\)-size nonuniform circuits, allowing the constant and starting length to depend on the function. A fixed constant-factor lower bound does not establish the target. Nor does a lower bound only for formulas, monotone circuits, XOR-only circuits or a fixed depth bound without a proof extending it to unrestricted circuits. The claim is unconditional, and an oracle-relative or conditional separation alone does not settle it. All complexity and quantifier requirements are exact; no numerical acceptance tolerance applies.
why: A superlinear lower bound would establish a basic limitation on unrestricted nonuniform computation for an efficiently computable function. It would surpass every fixed linear gate count, even when a circuit can reuse work freely across outputs, and expose structure that simple counting does not identify.

importance.reason: A fundamental lower-bound milestone for unrestricted computation, with connections to matrix complexity, proof techniques and the limitations of nonuniform algorithms.

progress.text: Open Problem 5.8 states the explicit multi-output not-linear target; the card retains its earlier polynomial-time specialization.
Theorem 1.1 gives \(3.1n-o(n)\) full-basis circuit lower bounds for affine dispersers.
The covering paper relates circuit complexity and two-dimensional cover problems and establishes bounds for random graphs.
The gate-simplification work proves results for selected bases and a constructive form of a classical linear lower bound.
Corollaries 3 and 4 give conditional near-linear and linear-size barriers for matrix natural proofs, with explicit transfer to Boolean circuits.

status_note: Source-open with bounded later-work checking through 16 September 2026. The 2018 source formulation, Li–Yang Theorem 1.1 and basis, the 2025 cover-work introduction, the February 2026 gate-simplification abstract/introduction, and the July 2026 matrix-natural-proofs revision including Corollary 1’s proof and Corollaries 3–4 were read. These later works do not supply the requested superlinear unrestricted bound. No matching unconditional resolution was located; this does not independently verify every cited theorem or exhaust the literature. The polynomial-time specialization predates this review and remains explicitly distinguished from the source’s broader wording.

context_blocks.text: A circuit may reuse any intermediate result and share it among different outputs. Those permissions make it stronger than a formula, whose computation is organized as a tree. The question retains all this circuit power and asks for an efficiently computable function that cannot be implemented with a fixed number of gates per input bit.

Counting proves that most Boolean truth tables require exponentially many gates. It does not supply a function computable by one polynomial-time algorithm, so it does not satisfy this card’s explicitness requirement. The challenge is obtaining a size lower bound for a computationally accessible function.

Linear maps over \(\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}\), with addition modulo two, form a significant special case. An efficiently constructible binary matrix \(A_n\) defines \(F_n(x)=A_nx\). Counting gives matrices needing \(\Omega(n^2/\log n)\) gates, but the 2026 source still identifies a superlinear lower bound for explicit matrices as open. A lower bound for circuits using only XOR gates would not automatically apply to circuits with arbitrary Boolean gates.

The desired function already has polynomial-size circuits because its uniform polynomial-time computation can be simulated by circuits. The question therefore separates linear size from polynomial size within efficient computation. Such a lower bound alone is not a proof that \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\). Conversely, a hard NP language need not be polynomial-time computable and so need not meet this card’s explicitness condition.

Li and Yang prove a \(3.1n-o(n)\) lower bound for suitable affine dispersers in the full two-input Boolean basis. An affine disperser is nonconstant on every affine subspace above its specified dimension threshold; suitable examples are polynomial-time computable. This is a substantial improvement of the known linear constant, while every fixed constant remains compatible with \(O(n)\) circuits.

The 2025 covering paper relates circuit lower bounds to combinatorial cover complexity and proves bounds for random graphs. Its results do not exhibit a polynomial-time function with the superlinear unrestricted circuit lower bound requested here.

The February 2026 gate-elimination preprint gives formal simplification results for selected bases and an efficiently checkable form of a classical linear parity lower bound. Its additional proof structure does not supply a superlinear unrestricted bound.

Raz’s July 2026 revision proves conditional barriers for matrix natural proofs: proofs identifying a sufficiently large set of hard matrices recognizable in time polynomial in the matrix description. Under the cryptographic assumptions stated in that paper, pseudorandom matrices with small circuits obstruct this defined proof class. The near-linear and linear circuit-size barriers rely on different assumptions; neither rules out all possible proofs of this card’s target.

sentences: The question asks for a polynomial-time computable function with as many output bits as input bits that needs more than linear circuit size.
Competing circuits may use every two-input Boolean operation and share intermediate work without depth or fan-out restrictions.
The lower-bound ratio must be unbounded at arbitrarily large input lengths, not necessarily tend to infinity at every length.
Known explicit full-basis lower bounds improve fixed linear constants, and recent conditional barriers apply only to specified proof classes.
A complete answer must prove or refute the existence of one uniformly computable function satisfying the entire claim.
